compositionNote: A child (子) is sheltered under a roof (宀), just as a written character shelters and carries meaning.
poem: Under a roof, snug and small,
a child learns to write it all.
Stroke by stroke, a mark, a sign —
that's a CHARACTER (zì), yours and mine.

compositionNote: A precious jade (玉) guarded within an enclosure (囗) pictures the treasured land of a country.
poem: Inside four walls, a jewel of jade,
guarded well, its worth displayed.
Borders drawn, a realm construed —
that's a COUNTRY (guó), whole and true.

meanings.def: the Han people; Chinese (as in 汉语, 汉字)

components.meaning: hand; again — used here as a sound hint

compositionNote: The water radical (氵), from the Han River, combines with 又 as a sound hint to give hàn — the Han people and their language.
poem: By the river, hands at play,
Han folk lived along its way.
Their name in flowing water again —
say HAN (hàn), the people of the plain.

components.meaning: I; me — used here as a sound hint

compositionNote: Speech (讠) plus 吾 (‘I/me’, a sound hint) forms yǔ — the words that come out when a person speaks: language.
poem: Words pour out when 'I' would speak,
sentences form, week by week.
Sound and tongue, in speech imbued —
that's LANGUAGE (yǔ), spoken and construed.

components.meaning: a pictograph of crossed decorative lines, like a pattern tattooed on a chest

compositionNote: 文 pictures crossed ornamental lines — the ancient image of pattern and marking that grew into ‘writing’ and ‘culture’.
poem: Crossed lines etched on ancient skin,
patterns marking where art begins.
From old tattoos, this sign was spun —
that's WRITING (wén), and culture as one.

compositionNote: Crossed strokes on top (representing guiding hands) sit above a cover (冖) and a child (子) — hands guiding a child under a roof to learn.
poem: Hands up above reach down with care,
guiding a child 'neath the roof up there.
Lesson by lesson, day by day —
that's how we LEARN (xué) and find our way.

meanings.def: to be born; to give birth to

components.meaning: a pictograph of a tender shoot pushing up out of the ground

compositionNote: 生 pictures a young shoot breaking through the soil — the image of birth, growth, and life.
poem: A tender shoot breaks through the ground,
pushing up without a sound.
New and green, it starts to grow —
that's LIFE (shēng) beginning, don't you know.

meanings.def: prefix showing familiarity or respect, e.g. 老师, 老朋友

components.meaning: long hair of an elderly person (a variant of 老)
a bent figure, like a person leaning on a cane

compositionNote: 老 pictures an elderly person with long hair (耂) bent over like a cane (匕) — the image of old age.
poem: Long white hair, a bended cane,
walking slow through wind and rain.
Wisdom carried, year by year —
that's OLD (lǎo) age, drawing near.

meanings.def: specialist; expert (in compounds like 医师)

components.meaning: an ancient sign for a mound of earth; troops stationed there

compositionNote: A flag (巾) planted beside a troop mound (𠂤) once marked an army's leader; the meaning shifted to a skilled leader — a teacher or master.
poem: A banner raised above the crowd,
leading troops, calling loud.
Now it guides young minds instead —
that's the TEACHER (shī), out ahead.

compositionNote: Under one covering frame (冂), everyone shares a single mouth or voice (口) — the picture of being together, the same.
poem: One roof covers everyone,
one mouth speaking, joined as one.
No two voices, just one tone —
that means SAME (tóng), never alone.

components.meaning: to cross; to exchange — used here as a sound hint

compositionNote: Wood (木, once wooden shackles for training) pairs with 交 as a sound hint to give xiào — the place where students are trained: school.
poem: Wood once bound a lesson tight,
crossed with rules to make it right.
Now it's where the students go —
that's the SCHOOL (xiào) where knowledge grows.

compositionNote: A pig (豕) kept under a roof (宀) pictures the ancient farming household — home and family.
poem: Under a roof, warm and dry,
a pig is kept, the years go by.
Where the hearth and heart are found —
that's your HOME (jiā), your family's ground.

components.meaning: used here purely as a sound hint

compositionNote: Father (父) pairs with 巴 purely as a sound hint to spell bà — dad.
poem: Father's hand held firm and true,
巴 just lends the sound to you.
Call him loud, call him near —
that's DAD (bà), forever here.

components.meaning: horse — used here as a sound hint

compositionNote: Woman (女) plus 马 as a sound hint gives mā — mom.
poem: A woman riding on a horse,
galloping home, of course, of course.
Fast and warm, she comes to greet —
that's MOM (mā), so kind and sweet.

meanings.def: retroflex suffix -r attached to nouns (erhua), e.g. 花儿

components.meaning: a pictograph of a pair of legs, representing a person or child

compositionNote: 儿 pictures a pair of little legs — the simplified image of a young child.
poem: Just two little legs on the run,
scampering off before they're done.
Small and quick, this little one —
that's a CHILD (ér), full of fun.

components.meaning: a pictograph of a woman kneeling gracefully with arms folded

compositionNote: 女 pictures a woman kneeling gracefully with arms crossed — the ancient image of a woman.
poem: Kneeling gently, arms held low,
grace and calm in every bow.
An ancient picture, soft and clear —
that's WOMAN (nǚ), drawn right here.

meanings.def: noun suffix attached to many nouns, e.g. 桌子, 孩子

components.meaning: a pictograph of a swaddled baby with arms outstretched

compositionNote: 子 pictures a baby wrapped in a blanket with arms reaching out — the image of a child.
poem: Wrapped up snug in a blanket tight,
tiny arms reach for the light.
Bundled small, held with love —
that's a CHILD (zǐ), sent from above.

meanings.def: friend (bound form, used mainly in 朋友)

components.meaning: originally a string of paired cowrie shells, not the moon
a matching second string of shells

compositionNote: 朋 originally pictured two strings of cowrie shells tied together — things paired side by side, later meaning companions.
poem: Two strings of shells, side by side,
tied together, matched with pride.
Paired as one, wherever we roam —
that's a FRIEND (péng), your second home.

compositionNote: Two hands (又 and 又) reaching out and clasping together picture friendship — being of one mind with someone.
poem: One hand reaches, then another,
clasped together like a brother.
Side by side, we walk life's road —
that's a FRIEND (yǒu), sharing the load.

components.meaning: a modified form of 之/止, meaning a foot stepping forward

compositionNote: A foot stepping out (top strokes) ahead of a person's legs (儿) shows someone moving out in front — first, before.
poem: A foot steps out ahead of the rest,
past the legs, it leads the quest.
Out in front, before the crowd —
that means FIRST (xiān), stepping proud.

compositionNote: An arrow (矢, once used to probe wounds) kept in a case (匚) pictures the tools of healing — medicine.
poem: An arrow kept inside a case,
once used to heal, to probe, to trace.
Tools for tending every ill —
that's MEDICINE (yī), and healing skill.

components.meaning: complete — used here as a sound hint

compositionNote: A walled enclosure (阝) pairs with 完 as a sound hint to give yuàn — a courtyard, and by extension an institution like a hospital.
poem: A wall stands round, complete and whole,
enclosing a yard, a healing goal.
Step inside its gated door —
that's the COURTYARD (yuàn), and so much more.

compositionNote: 商 pictures a trader standing (立) on a tall stall, calling out (口) to advertise his wares — commerce, business.
poem: Standing tall upon his stand,
calling loud across the land.
Selling wares from dawn to night —
that's COMMERCE (shāng), a merchant's sight.

components.meaning: to occupy; to claim a spot

compositionNote: A building (广) where someone has staked out a spot (占) to sell goods — a shop.
poem: A building where a spot's been claimed,
goods on shelves, all neatly named.
Open the door and step on in —
that's the SHOP (diàn) where sales begin.

components.meaning: evolved from a net (网) cast over shells/money (贝) — reaching out to acquire goods

compositionNote: 买's shape comes from a net (网) held over money or shells (贝) — the ancient image of gathering goods to buy.
poem: A net cast wide, a coin below,
reaching out for what you owe.
Hand it over, take it home —
that's to BUY (mǎi), no need to roam.

components.meaning: a worn-down form of 出 (‘to go out’)

compositionNote: 卖 stacks 十 (a simplified form of 出, ‘to go out’) on top of 买 (‘to buy’) — sending goods out to be bought: to sell.
poem: Stack 十 on top of buying's frame,
sending goods out, just the same.
Out the door, into the crowd —
that's to SELL (mài), announced out loud.

components.meaning: metal — early coins were cast in bronze
small; piled up — used here as a sound and meaning hint

compositionNote: Metal (钅), since coins were cast in bronze, combines with 戋 (small bits piled up) as a sound hint to give qián — money.
poem: Metal melted, coins piled small,
counted careful, one and all.
Jingling pockets, spend with care —
that's the MONEY (qián) that we share.

components.meaning: to break off; decisive — used here as a sound hint

compositionNote: A clump of earth (土) broken off (夬) pictures a piece or chunk — and casually, a dollar.
poem: A clump of earth, broken free,
counted out for you and me.
One small chunk, or coins you keep —
that's a PIECE (kuài), never cheap.

components.meaning: a pictograph of a tall multi-story tower — roof on top, window in the middle, doorway below

compositionNote: 高 pictures a tall tower: a roof on top, a window in the middle, and a doorway (口) at the base — giving the meaning ‘tall, high’.
poem: A tower stands with roof on top,
windows, doorway, doesn't stop.
Reaching upward, proud and bold —
that's so HIGH (gāo), a sight to behold.

meanings.def: happy; in high spirits (as in 高兴)

components.meaning: simplified from 興, a picture of four hands raising an object together

compositionNote: 兴 comes from 興, a picture of four hands lifting something up together — the shared lift of excitement and interest.
poem: Four hands lift something up in glee,
raising joy for all to see.
Shared delight, a common cheer —
that's feeling EXCITED (xìng), joy sincere.

meanings.def: to like; to be fond of

components.meaning: a drum set on a stand

compositionNote: 喜 pictures a drum (壴) being beaten while a joyful mouth (口) sings along — the image of joy and happiness.
poem: A drum beats loud, a joyful sound,
mouths sing along, all around.
Celebration fills the air —
that's pure HAPPINESS (xǐ), everywhere.

components.meaning: hand — a remnant of the original phonetic 雚
a person with mouth wide open, as if yawning or exhaling

compositionNote: A hand (又, a remnant of the original phonetic 雚) beside a person with mouth wide open (欠) pictures joyful shouting — to be happy.
poem: A mouth flung open, shouting cheer,
hands clapping loud, drawing near.
Laughter rises, joy on tap —
that's being HAPPY (huān), joy's own lap.

meanings.def: to love; to be fond of

components.meaning: a hand reaching down, like a claw

compositionNote: A hand reaches down (爫) and shelters (冖) a friend (友) — simplified 爱 famously left out the heart (心) from the middle, yet still means love.
poem: A hand reaches down, a cover spread,
holding a friend close instead.
No heart drawn in, yet still it's true —
that's called LOVE (ài), given to you.

meanings.def: to visit; to see (a doctor, a friend)

components.meaning: hand, drawn here without its hook

compositionNote: A hand (手) shading the eyes (目) pictures someone peering into the distance — to look, to see.
poem: A hand shades the eye from the sun,
peering far till the searching's done.
Watching close, near and far —
that's to LOOK (kàn) at where things are.

meanings.def: to see; to catch sight of

compositionNote: An eye (目) sitting on top of a pair of legs (儿) pictures a person looking out — to see, to meet.
poem: An eye sits high on walking legs,
scanning round, no room for dregs.
Spotting friends out on the street —
that's to SEE (jiàn), and then to meet.

components.meaning: axe — used here as a sound hint

compositionNote: A mouth (口) paired with 斤 as a sound hint gives tīng — to listen, to hear.
poem: A mouth leans in, an axe rings clear,
sound waves travel to the ear.
Quiet now, and lend an ear —
that's to LISTEN (tīng), far and near.
